territorial_scope.description: Federal statute of the United States that amends the Small Business Act and applies to SBA 7(a) loans.

evidence.quote: Be it enacted by the Senate and House of Representatives of the United States of America in Congress assembled,

summary.short: Amends Section 7(a) of the Small Business Act so the Administration may make loans for business software or cloud computing services, including AI-based business tools, covering functions such as payroll, sales, billing and accounting. Introduced bill; the text states no effective date.
summary.long: The Small Business Technological Act of 2025 (S.305, introduced) amends Section 7(a) of the Small Business Act (15 U.S.C. 636(a)) by adding a new paragraph (38). Under the new paragraph, the Administration may provide 7(a) loans, in whole or in part, to finance business software or cloud computing services, or any technology that facilitates business operations, product or service delivery, payroll processing, payment or tracking, human resources, sales and billing, or accounting, inventory, records and expenses. The paragraph expressly includes business tools that utilize artificial intelligence. A rule of construction provides that the amendment does not make earlier 7(a) loans for these purposes impermissible, does not authorize using 7(a) loans for research and development, and does not limit the definition of working capital under the Small Business Act. The bill's text sets no eligibility thresholds, penalties or effective date. The registry records its status as pending, at the introduced stage.

relations.note: Adds new paragraph (38) to section 7(a) authorizing SBA loans to finance business software and cloud computing services, including business tools that utilize artificial intelligence.
